To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully designed a novel strategy of combined application of siRNA and chemotherapeutics by multi-functional NPs for simultaneous inhibition of tumor angiogenesis and tumor cell proliferation.

co-delivery of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor siRNA (si-VEGF) and chemotherapeutic agent Etoposide (ETO), using multi-functional nanoparticles (PHCL-NPs), simultaneously inhibits tumor proliferation and tumor vascularization, resulting in more significant inhibition of tumor growth and distant metastasis than monotherapies.

we have designed and evaluated a multi-functional NPs co-delivered siVEGF and etoposide for the first time to achieve simultaneous targeting of tumor angiogenesis and tumor proliferation for enhanced anti-angiogenesis and anti-prolization effect on orthotopic NSLC treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and efficient combined therapy for orthotopic non-small cell lung tumor via co-delivering siRNA and chemotherapeutic drugs by multi-functional nanoparticles.
a novel strategy of combined therapy by co-delivering VEGF siRNAs and ETO for orthotopic lung tumors.

the development of a novel therapy strategy for orthotopic non-small cell lung tumor via co-delivery of siVEGF, which is a potent anti-angiogenic gene, and chemotherapeutic ETO by multi-functional NPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-delivery of siVEGF with chemotherapeutic agents ETO by multi-functional nanoparticles for orthotopic lung cancer therapy has been demonstrated for the first time.
the co-delivery of siVEGF with ETO by the PHCL-coated NPs with on-demand properties exhibited superior antitumor effect in the orthotopic model of NSCLC.

the combined application of anti-angiogenesis and anti-prolifteration via co-delivering siRNA and ETO via multi-functional NPs exhibited the desired antiproliferation and anti-angiogenesis efficacy in orthotopic NSLC treatment, which has significant potential in improving the therapeutic efficacy for the treatment of highly malignant and metastasis NSCLC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed an intelligent co-delivery system for combined anti-angiogenic therapy and chemotherapy regimen to treat highly metastatic and malignant non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) by targeting tumor proliferation and angiogenic signaling pathways.
we designed, for the fist time, a rational strategy via intelligently delivering siVEGF and etoposide by multi-functional nanoparticles directed against the orthotropic NSCLC.

the combined therapy by siRNA and chemotherapeutics co-delivered multi-functional NPs for orthotropic NSCLC simultaneously inhibits tumor proliferation and tumor neovascularization resulting in significant suppression of tumor metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have demonstrated the feasibility and potential of combined therapy by VEGF siRNAs and chemotherapeutic agent Etoposide co-delivered by multi-functional nanoparticles to achieve the desired synergistic effect in orthotopic lung cancer treatment.

we have successfully developed a multi-functional NPs co-delivery system with tailor-made surface charge features for enhanced tumor targeting, improved intracellular drug release, and excellent anti-angiogenesis and anti-prolifersation efficiency in the orthotopic non-small cell lung tumor.
the combination of anti-angiogenic therapy and chemotherapy is a promising strategy for the treatment of highly malignant and metastasis lung tumor.
